summary: Round 5. The three survivors reported in round 4 are dead -- I re-measured each. The count sign half (0xFFFFFFFF_7FFFFFFF), the attributionLen sign half over podId AND the over-long half over incarnationId, and the pod-slot presence flag enumeration all kill their mutations. Every acceptance criterion now has a test that fails without the change: per-segment attribution (hoist dies), VERSION_ATTRIBUTED with an enumerated presence flag (both the flag mutation and the version range mutation die), neither legacy layout moved (both encode-version mutations die), CommitRequest.incarnationId refusal, and once-per-instance minting (both per-flush and constant mutations die). The four re-taken AttributedDeltaTest reds are honest: red.log shows real AssertionFailedError/AssertionError/IllegalStateException entries at the named line numbers, recorded from JUnit XML rather than a build failure, and check-tdd reports 31 new tests all observed failing first and unchanged since. No testing.md tier or hygiene violation: no Thread.sleep, no fixed port, no system temp, no mock, and no existing assertion was weakened -- I checked the CommitProtocolSimulationFlushSeqTest pair-to-triple widening by reverting the key to the old pair and it FAILS in the new simulation, so the widening is forced, not a rule-5 inversion. Two survivors remain, one of them on the untrusted decode path.

findings.title: SegmentCommit.Attribution's entire compact constructor is deletable with the whole build green -- and it sits on the untrusted decode path
findings.failure_scenario: CommitDelta.decodeAttributedBody builds `new SegmentCommit.Attribution(pod, inc, flushSeq)` directly from wire bytes (CommitDelta.java:231). A torn or foreign attributed delta whose podId length prefix is 0 yields podId="". Today the record refuses it and ChainEntry.decodeKinded wraps that into IOException; if the guard were wrong the delta decodes as VALID carrying a blank podId, and M4.10d's dedup -- which this whole commit exists to key -- collapses every node's commits into one identity. That is the exact harm CommitRequestTest.aBlankPodIdIsRefused already cites for the sibling API field, and this commit ADDED CommitRequestTest.aBlankOrNullIncarnationIsRefused for the same reason ('the new one arrived with a guard, a four-line comment and no case, and deleting the guard left the whole build green'). The identical situation now exists one class over, on the wire path rather than the API path, which is strictly more exposed. AttributedDeltaTest pins the LENGTH prefixes and the segment COUNT but never a VALUE the record refuses.
findings.surviving_mutation: Delete the whole `public Attribution { ... }` compact constructor from SegmentCommit.java:33-42 (null checks, blank check, flushSeq<0 check). MEASURED: `./gradlew :format:test :sequencer:test :ingest:test` -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL. Narrower: delete only the two lines `if (podId.isBlank() || incarnationId.isBlank()) { throw ... }`; I then built a delta by hand, rewrote its `04 'poda'` length prefix to `00`, and CommitDelta.decode returned a valid delta with podId=[] and no exception. With the guard present the same bytes give `java.io.IOException: corrupt chain entry of kind 3: podId and incarnationId are never blank`.
findings.suggested_test: In AttributedDeltaTest, splice a zero-length podId (and separately a zero-length incarnationId) over the fixture's prefix and assert IOException -- the same splice helper the length tests already use. A negative-reading flushSeq uvarint is the third case.

findings.title: The pointer's EPOCH half is unconstrained: every fixture that reaches CheckpointWriter runs at epoch 1, so a hard-coded 1 passes
findings.failure_scenario: The slot's pointer is (epoch, sequence) and ADR-0036's clause is that it names an ADDRESSABLE delta. The SEQUENCE half got a dedicated test this round after a measured off-by-one (theSlotPointsAtTheDeltaThatAppliedNotTheOneAfterIt, whose own javadoc records 'a delta at sequence 0 stored 1/1'). The EPOCH half has no equivalent. A checkpoint written by an epoch-4 leader that recorded epoch 1 points into another term's key space entirely; the production comment's own words for the sequence half -- 'Every checkpoint then pointed at an empty slot or an unrelated later delta, and a detected replay could not be answered at all' -- apply verbatim, and M4.10d is the consumer.
findings.surviving_mutation: `long pointerEpoch = log.epoch();` -> `long pointerEpoch = 1L;`. MEASURED: `./gradlew :sequencer:test` -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL. The two tests that touch epoch both pin the constant rather than the derivation: CheckpointWriterContentTest.java:79 asserts `slot.epoch()).isEqualTo(log.epoch())` on a fixture built as `new CommitLog(store, "bins", 1)`, and LocalSequencerCheckpointTest.java:116 asserts `s.epoch()).isEqualTo(1L)` literally. theFirstCheckpointAfterATakeoverCarriesNoPodsAtAll does run a successor at epoch 2 but asserts only doesNotContainKey.
findings.suggested_test: Extend theFirstCheckpointAfterATakeoverCarriesNoPodsAtAll, or add a case there: after `new CommitLog(store, "bins", 2).recover()` and a commit for podb, assert `pods().get("podb").epoch()` is 2, not 1. That is the only shape that tells log.epoch() from a constant.

findings.title: The 'still VERSION_DELTA' assertion reads the wrong byte and can never fail
findings.failure_scenario: The chain header is MAGIC (bytes 0-3) then a BIG-ENDIAN int version (bytes 4-7). `bytes[4]` is the version's HIGH byte, which is 0x00 for every version the codec can emit -- VERSION_DELTA=0 and VERSION_KINDED=1 alike. `assertThat(bytes[4]).isEqualTo((byte) ChainEntry.VERSION_DELTA)` therefore asserts 0==0 whatever version was written. GoldenAttributedTest.java:96 reads [7] for exactly this and is correct. The test's own red record confirms it: red.log shows this test went red on `IllegalStateException at AttributedDeltaTest.java:83`, i.e. inside encode(), so line 85 was never observed failing.
findings.surviving_mutation: Delete the `if (segments.size() == 1) { ... VERSION_DELTA ... }` branch from CommitDelta.encode so an unattributed one-segment delta emits the v1 KINDED batched layout instead. MEASURED: `./gradlew :format:test --tests binjava.format.AttributedDeltaTest` -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL, the class is entirely green including this assertion. The full suite catches it only via pre-existing BatchedCommitDeltaTest / ChainEntryTest / GoldenChainEntryTest, so this test contributes nothing to the version claim it advertises.

findings.title: The new mixed-attribution IllegalStateException in writeAttribution has no test
findings.failure_scenario: encode() decides `attributed` from ANY segment carrying attribution, then writeAttribution refuses a null one so a delta cannot be half-attributed. If that refusal were dropped, encoding a delta whose segments are partly attributed silently emits a stream missing one triple, and the decoder then reads the NEXT segment's key length as a podId length -- a self-consistently corrupt object rather than a caller error at the point of the mistake. Not reachable from CommitLog or FakeSequencer today (both attribute all or none), but CommitDelta and SegmentCommit are public API in :format: and the guard is new in this commit.
findings.surviving_mutation: `if (a == null) { throw new IllegalStateException(...); }` -> `if (a == null) { return; }`. MEASURED: `./gradlew :format:test :sequencer:test` -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL. No fixture anywhere builds a mixed delta.
findings.suggested_test: One case in AttributedDeltaTest: `new CommitDelta(1, List.of(seg("a",...), new SegmentCommit("b", runs))).encode()` throws IllegalStateException.

findings.title: This test's stated reason was made false by this same commit, and it is the prose an M4.10d session reads
findings.failure_scenario: The leading comment says '`CommitDelta` carries (sequence, segments) and nothing else, so a new leader cannot recover `lastAppliedFlushSeq` from the chain', and the assertion's as() message at :229 says poda's flushSeq 'is nowhere on the chain'. Both are now FALSE: the helper commits via log.commitAll, so the epoch-1 delta carries Attribution("poda","i1",42) and the watermark IS on the chain. The BEHAVIOUR asserted is still real -- the writer does not yet rebuild from the tail, which is M4.10d -- but the justification is the exact premise ADR-0036 reversed, and CheckpointWriter's own javadoc three files away now says the opposite ('THE PER-POD SLOT IS NO LONGER PROCESS-LOCAL, and this paragraph used to say the opposite'). The task packet's whole point about the seam javadocs is that an M4.10d session reads the seam, not the backlog; this test comment is part of that seam and was missed by the sweep that fixed CheckpointWriter, CommitLog, Sequencer and FakeSequencer.
findings.surviving_mutation: No production mutation -- this is a false claim in a test comment, not a weak assertion. The assertion itself (doesNotContainKey) is correct and I verified it is not weakened relative to HEAD.
findings.suggested_test: Reword to say what is now true: the attribution IS on the chain, and the writer does not yet read it back -- M4.10d does. Then the test still fails if the writer ever starts pre-populating pods, which is what it is for.
